title: Rearrange a formula for one variable
subtitle: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  · 33 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **33 of the official questions in Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  are this one** — 11 Easy, 15 Medium, 7 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The equation relates several letters, often a named real-world formula with fractions, reciprocals or a squared variable.
- The question asks 'which equation expresses X in terms of...' or 'which is equivalent to X', and every choice is an expression in the other letters.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Clear the fractions by multiplying through by the common denominator.
- 2) Collect every term containing the target variable on one side, factor that variable out if it appears more than once, then divide.
- 3) If the target is squared, take the square root and use the stated positivity to keep only the positive root.
- If you solved for 1/X, take reciprocals at the end.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Usually slow, but it works as a check: pick numbers for all the other variables, compute the target from the original equation, and see which choice gives the same value.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You 'undo' a sum of fractions term by term, for example flipping 1/a + 1/b into a + b, or you divide before collecting the target variable's terms.
You might also forget the reciprocal step or drop a subtraction's sign while isolating.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
